title: Tech Noir
description: Tech noir (also called future noir or cyber-noir) fuses noir's hard keys, rain, and guilty blocking with science-fiction production design: screens, LEDs, and corporate towers as practical sources. Analog crime grammar sits inside a digital city.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: The future is wet and guilty. A detective, a fugitive, or a machine walks rain that is lit by advertisements and monitors.
The face is still half in shadow. The key is no longer only a streetlamp.
It is a billboard, a terminal, a police scanner. It is not all dystopia and not all neo-noir.
Dystopian can be daylight bureaucracy and civic scale with no crime plot. Neo-Noir can be a present-day parking garage with sodium lamps and no future tech.
Tech noir needs both the investigation geometry and the machine city.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Keep noir ratios: hard key, unfilled cheek, wet ground. Replace tungsten with screens and LEDs as motivated keys, plus residual sodium or neon.
Smoke or rain for volume. 35mm or 40mm anamorphic, night exteriors, occasional long-lens compression of towers.
Blocking: figures small under signage, then a close-up keyed by a display. Prompt future crime, screens as practicals, rain, corporate night, analog noir in a digital city.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it when a future city is also a crime scene and the screens light the guilt. Do not use it for a clean utopian interface, or for present-day noir with no speculative design.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: Tech Noir is noir plus science-fiction sources. Neo-Noir is color noir without requiring future tech.
Dystopian is the used civic system, often in daylight, with the state as antagonist. Neon Practicals is the lamp.
Film Noir is the silver ancestor. If there is no screen, tower, or machine as light, you are still in neo-noir.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is Neo-Noir or generic Dystopian: contemporary neon crime, or a grey megacity with no investigation geometry. The tell is no screen as a source, or daylight civic haze with no wet guilty night.
Fix: add a display key, rain, towers, and a crime blocking of isolation.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Tech Noir in film?

A fusion of noir lighting and crime structure with science-fiction design. Screens and corporate night become the practicals. Rain stays. Guilt stays. The city is digital. The grammar is still investigation.
Tech Noir vs Neo-Noir
Neo-noir is color noir in a later or present world. Tech noir requires speculative technology as light and as threat. Blade Runner is both. A 2010s parking-garage crime film may be neo-noir only.
When should I use Tech Noir?
When the future is a wet crime scene and a screen lights the face. Skip it for silver 1940s noir, for daylight civic dystopia, or for pastel vaporwave with no investigation.
How do I prompt Tech Noir for AI image or video?
Write: Tech-noir on [Subject], future crime, screens as practicals, rain, corporate night, hard unfilled key. Name the display. Do not stop at neon rain with no speculative city.
